correctness.rationale: The smooth projective scroll in Piene--Shapiro gives a proper birational map. The explicit coefficient map recovers any nonzero image polynomial from finitely many factor degrees, making it quasi-finite and hence finite, so it is the normalization. Pullback of the leading-coefficient hyperplane is V(a)+2V(c), with birational images a plane and the irreducible cubic E^3-4DEF+8D^2G. Its plane intersection is 2ell+m. Two generic preimages on each line prove nonnormality, while every other image point has one preimage with rank-three Jacobian in the exhibited charts; these give the entire reduced singular locus. The general effective boundary cycles follow from the same bundle and Segre classes, not finite empirical tests. check.py confirms critical identities but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Piene--Shapiro explicitly leave the behavior at infinity as a separate geometric problem. The calculation finds the complete nonnormal singular support and exact doubled cubic boundary in the first nonlinear degree-seven compactification, distinguishing it structurally from the smooth affine locus. The general boundary cycle explains a natural Stirling recursion and predicts multiplicities relevant to intersection theory and degenerations; this is not an arbitrary numerical slice or just degree recomputation.
